newSince0809: TICKETS FOR 10 SEPTEMBER TO 31 DECEMBER 2026 HAVE SOLD OUT. The museum states this plainly. This is the single most useful new fact for October: a reader arriving in October cannot buy a ticket for their trip, only for January to March 2027. The October guide should lead with that, not with the release dates alone.
Members' priority booking for April to July 2027 opens January 2027; the general release for April to July 2027 opens 'early 2027'.
Schools bookings for January to March 2027 open 29 September 2026. Patrons and Supporters also open 29 September 2026 - both BEFORE the members' date, and both in September rather than October.
Reciprocal entry and passes from ICOM, ICOMOS, MA and NMDC are NOT valid for the Bayeux Tapestry between September and December 2026. 2027 arrangements to be announced.
Maximum 10 tickets per booking. Multiple bookings from the same email address will be cancelled. Tickets can only be used by the booker and ID may be checked.
Tickets are emailed four days in advance of the visit.

prices.standard: Adults £33 (£36.50 with the £3.50 donation). Under 16s free, booked alongside an accompanying adult, maximum four per adult. Students, 16-18s and jobseekers £25. Disabled visitors £25 with a free assistant, booking required. National Art Pass £16.50.

bayeuxTickets.visitDetail: Allow 40 minutes. Entry is timed and follows a one-way route. Photography permitted but no flash; drawing and sketching are not permitted. bayeuxOpeningFestival.what: THE BAYEUX TAPESTRY OPENING FESTIVAL - free, 9 to 11 October 2026, and completely absent from the 8 September stub. This is the answer to the sold-out problem: three days of free Bayeux programming at the British Museum that anyone can attend without a Tapestry ticket.

events.title: Bayeux Late: medieval making
events.detail: The first Bayeux Late and the start of the opening festival. Workshops and activities. Free to drop in at any time between 17.30 and 20.30; activities are non-ticketed, first-come first-served. Contributors include Matilda Ngute of The Textile Club, Olivia Swarthout of Weird Medieval Guys, and master embroidery artist Bella Lane.

events.title: Big Bayeux Bash
events.detail: A weekend of free family activities inspired by the medieval world - workshops and drop-in sessions for children aged six and over and their adults. Different activities on specific days. Non-ticketed, first-come first-served.

bayeuxOpeningFestival.criticalCaveat: NEITHER EVENT INCLUDES ENTRY TO THE BAYEUX TAPESTRY. The museum says so explicitly on both pages: tickets must be booked separately. Print this or readers will turn up on 9 October expecting to see the Tapestry. Visitors are advised to book a free timed Museum entry ticket for priority entry during busy periods; the main entrance is on Great Russell Street and there is a security and bag check.
bayeuxOpeningFestival.why: A free, dated, three-day event at the biggest cultural draw in the city, in a month when its tickets are sold out. Nothing else in October is this useful to a reader who has already missed the boat.

theatreSource.why: Official London Theatre is the Society of London Theatre's own non-profit ticketing platform - the industry body, not a reseller. Its listing pages embed schema.org TheaterEvent JSON-LD with exact startDate, endDate, venue, postcode and lowPrice per show, which is why every entry above carries a venue and a price. This solves the theatre-closing-dates-source item in data/worklist.json: SOLT's last-chance URL 404s, but the last_chance FILTER on the ticketing listing works.
theatreSource.criticalCaveat: OLT's endDate IS NOT ALWAYS A CLOSING DATE. For an open-ended long-runner it is the end of the current BOOKING PERIOD. Moulin Rouge! The Musical appears in the last_chance filter with endDate 2026-10-17, which would read as a closing - but its own OLT show page is labelled 'Booking Until' and offers performances on 1, 8 and 15 December 2026, and the producer's site says the Piccadilly run releases one additional week of performances every Monday. It is NOT closing on 17 October and has been excluded. The tell is the run length: a show whose startDate is years back is showing you a booking horizon. Every entry in theatreClosing above is a limited run that began in 2026, and the two Globe shows were additionally confirmed on the Globe's own site.
theatreSource.stillToDo: The above is discovery plus JSON-LD. Anything given real prominence in the article should be confirmed at the producing theatre's own site, as the Globe pair and Moulin Rouge were.

flagsForHuman: MOULIN ROUGE! IS THE NEAR-MISS OF THIS PASS. It sits in Official London Theatre's 'Last Chance To See' filter with an end date of 17 October 2026. It is not closing. Its own OLT page is labelled 'Booking Until' and sells performances on 1, 8 and 15 December, and the producer releases another week of performances every Monday. Had this been printed it would have been the worst error in the guide. Excluded. The general lesson is in theatreSource.criticalCaveat.

lessonsForNextMonth: A LISTING'S END DATE IS NOT ALWAYS A CLOSING DATE. Official London Theatre's last_chance filter mixes genuine final performances with booking horizons for open-ended runs. Check the run length: a show that started years ago and appears to close in five weeks is showing you its booking window.

THE VENUE'S OWN SITE BEATS THE TRACKER, AND SOMETIMES CONTRADICTS IT. Bar Douro had moved to November, Bamboo Mat's address was wrong, Dishoom calls its own site Borough rather than London Bridge. All three would have been printed wrong from Hot Dinners alone.

HOT DINNERS HAS A 'COMING SOON' GUIDE WITH A PER-MONTH SECTION - hot-dinners.com/Features/Articles/coming-soon-new-restaurants-opening-in-london. It is the right page for a monthly guide; the Latest news feed that September used is a fire-hose of the last fortnight.

THE NEW-VENUE PASS WORKS AND SHOULD BE STANDING. Searching deliberately for openings that are neither restaurants nor gigs found Absurd City, the Lightroom show and EbonyLife Place - none of which would surface from Hot Dinners or a venue's what's-on page. Blue Note was the September lesson; this month it paid off.
CHECK WHAT AN INSTITUTION CALLS A THING. Two entries in the stub's exhibition-closing list turned out to be a short course and a selling display. The RA's own site labels each category explicitly.

SEARCH ENGINES: DuckDuckGo HTML and Mojeek both rate-limited or served a captcha after a handful of curl queries on 9 September. Google via the browser pane worked throughout and is the reliable route for SERP-first discovery here.
